evals.prompt: Show the native Nautilus Rust 0.64.0 bracket-order creation and submission sequence for a Strategy. Explain leg types and contingent defaults. When must local IDs and possible-send state be recorded? Do not connect or place a real order.
evals.expected_output: A source-compatible order().bracket().call() and submit_order_list sequence, with pre-submit bookkeeping and qualified contingent semantics.
assertions: Uses order().bracket() and submit_order_list, recognizing call() returns Vec<OrderAny> ordered entry, stop-loss, take-profit.
Records leg IDs and possible-send/reservation bookkeeping before submission because dispatch can be synchronous.
Identifies OTO entry, reduce-only exits and default OUO, not default OCO; does not claim universal broker protection.
Keeps risk bypass false and does not treat a submit error as proof of no send.

evals.prompt: A Nautilus Rust order is pending cancel when a partial fill arrives. Later a cancellation event is followed by another fill. I want to release all reserved capital when I request cancel, and read final Portfolio totals in on_order_filled. Is that sound?
evals.expected_output: Reject premature release and final-Portfolio assumptions; derive state from native fills and confirmed remaining exposure.
assertions: Pending cancel/update can coexist with partial fills and canceled orders can receive late fills.
Does not release all reservation merely on a cancellation request or assume a canceled status excludes later fills.
Distinguishes updated Cache order/position state from Portfolio aggregation that follows position-event handling.

evals.prompt: I only need to load Databento historical bars into a Nautilus catalog, with symbol and timestamp normalization. No strategy or orders. Which workflow should own the task?
evals.expected_output: Choose integrating-nautilus-data, without expanding into strategy risk or order implementation.
assertions: Assigns ingestion, catalog and identity/timestamp work to the data integration workflow.
Does not introduce Strategy, orders or broker execution for this data-only task.
